Where natural hot springs existed (as in Bath, England; Băile Herculane, Romania or Aquae Calidae near Burgas and Serdica, Bulgaria) thermae were built around them.", "reason": "The page documents widespread Roman public baths across the empire, including European locations, substantiating that Romans built bathhouses in Europe long before the Moors (though it gives no '711' date or 'thousands' figure)."}

parsed.note_claim: Romans built thousands of public bathhouses across Europe centuries before the Moors arrived in Iberia in 711 AD.
parsed.label: SUPPORTS
parsed.quote: Baths sprang up all over the empire. Where natural hot springs existed (as in Bath, England; Băile Herculane, Romania or Aquae Calidae near Burgas and Serdica, Bulgaria) thermae were built around them.
parsed.reason: The page documents widespread Roman public baths across the empire, including European locations, substantiating that Romans built bathhouses in Europe long before the Moors (though it gives no '711' date or 'thousands' figure).
